items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: I never saw Billie on stage with Artie Shaw for example

ctx.x: But it doesn’t matter. And the great breakthrough came about in the middle 30s when Benny Goodman hired Teddy Wilson to play as a member of the first Goodman trio that started on records actually. But Goodman decided we’re going to do this in person. So what he did was to play a set and maybe twice an evening, they would do this at the end of the set there would be a brief break and out would come the trio with Teddy replacing Jess Stacy on piano and Gene Krupa returning to the drums, and they would play maybe…
It wasn’t just in the south either, was it? © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

items.title: Avakian George — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He’s the daddy, like Billie Holiday. “I’m as close as I can get to Louis Armstrong,” she would say.

ctx.x: This was in 1940, probably in the spring of 1940. I got to chatting with him. I don’t remember what we talked about, but he was a very amusing guy. He made a series of records on Vocalion, 35-cent specials – not specials, but 35-cent pickup dates like

Billie Holiday and Fats Waller on Victor and so forth, except Fats had a permanent band, because he was a star. Then, when Louis’s friends left, the bartender or somebody said, “Louis’s alone in the back, and he knows that someone wants to see him. Go back there.” I walked up to him and introduced myself. Wow, what a moment. Wow, Louis Armstrong, the man that I had heard as well as bought records of, and now I was prepared to tell him, “Louis, here’s some things that you did when you were young, you don’t know…
